headline: Roman soldiers were not paid in salt — the "salary" story has no ancient evidence
summary: "Salary" comes from Latin salarium, linked to sal, salt — but no ancient source documents Roman soldiers actually being paid in salt. Pliny the Elder (1st century AD) links salt to official posts and the word's origin, without describing a salt-payment practice (his exact wording is still being pinned down — do not quote him directly yet). The "soldiers paid in salt" story traces to an 18th-century Latin dictionary (Facciolati–Forcellini, 1771), which guessed it by analogy with words like calcearium, "shoe money." A 1st-century-AD source (Smith's Dictionary, 1875) describes the Augustan-era salarium as paid in money, not salt.
